description: Eight voices of two oscillators each, every one running into a tuned feedback comb and modulated by whichever other voice it is pointed at, with sixty-four values drawn as bars

params.text: Chooses which of the eight values per voice the bars show: pitch, the FM source, amplitude, the AM source, the filter corner, the filter type, the delay time, or the feedback
Chooses how a voice is built: a pulse oscillator filtered inside the loop, a pulse oscillator filtered before it, or a parabolic oscillator with no filter at all
Chooses what dragging in the bar area does: draw the bars by hand, wrap them round, or scatter them at random
Maps all eight pitch bars at once: everything but the top of the bank crushed down fully anticlockwise, the bars exactly as drawn at noon, the whole bank lifted fully clockwise
Maps all eight filter-corner bars in the same three-curve way, crushed fully anticlockwise, as drawn at noon, lifted fully clockwise
Maps all eight delay-time bars in the same three-curve way, crushed fully anticlockwise, as drawn at noon, lifted fully clockwise
Moves five settings at once: the frequency modulation ratio 1 to 16, the amplitude modulation depth 0 to 5, every filter's resonance 0.95 down to 0.30, a smoothing multiplier and the normaliser floor
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the knob above
Scatters all sixty-four values at random; the maker's own warning about unexpected bursts of noise applies, so turn the level down first
Sends all sixty-four values off towards new destinations while it is held down, arriving together after the time set beside it and immediately leaving again
Sets how long each leg of a morph takes, 0.1 seconds to 30 seconds; it is a time to arrive rather than a rate, and a change takes effect at the start of the next leg

inputs.text: Added to the pitch mapping knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the cutoff mapping knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the delay mapping knob through the attenuverter beside it
Added to the flow knob through the attenuverter beside it
A signal injected into every loop at once, filtered, delayed, saturated and cross-modulated by the bank, and taken up into what the bank modulates itself with
A rising edge scatters all sixty-four values at random
While it is high all sixty-four values set off towards new destinations, as the morph button does

outputs.text: The first oscillator of each of the eight voices summed, through the output fader; there is no panning, and the two sides differ because their modulation comes from opposite ends of the bank
The second oscillator of each of the eight voices summed, through the output fader
The bank's own slow wander, ±5V: the sixteen oscillator levels summed with alternating sign and low-passed at 25Hz, so common motion cancels and what is left is how unevenly they are behaving

notes: the sixty-four bars in the edit area are not reachable from this help: they are drawn as one display widget rather than as sixty-four controls.
the bars are real parameters all the same, saved with the patch and randomised with the module.
a bar is edited by dragging in that area, and what dragging does is set by the edit switch. The function switch chooses which eight of the sixty-four are on screen.
the square to the right of the bars is a Lissajous of the two outputs: one closed loop means the bank is behaving, a filled square means it has gone to noise.
this plays itself. With nothing patched the bank oscillates, and the level knob is where to start.
